purpose: Provide a session-bounded, fine-grained ontology of IR indexing data structures and construction methods (inverted index, postings compression, skip pointers, positional/phrase indexes, impact/tiered indexes, batch/distributed/dynamic construction, pruning, forward index, suffix arrays, wavelet trees, n-gram/wildcard indexes, signature files, caching) to plan, evaluate, sequence, validate, and lock index designs that make retrieval fast and scalable.
assumptions: Parent domain is information_retrieval_and_search_systems; this KB models the indexing-structures subdomain at fine grain.
No observed dataset, benchmark, or expert-judgment input was supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Each node is a single fine-grained indexing structure or construction/serving method, sized for one heavy reasoning session.
Workload (corpus size, query mix, latency/size SLOs) is a parameter the workflow profiles before locking schema.
exclusions: Relevance ranking model design beyond what index layout requires (e.g., learning-to-rank training).
Crawling, parsing/tokenization linguistics, and query understanding beyond index-facing concerns.
Vector/ANN embedding indexes (HNSW/IVF) are out of scope; this KB covers classical text indexing structures.
Storage hardware and filesystem engineering beyond index layout implications.

glossary.definition: term-to-postings mapping enabling fast term lookup
per-term list of docIDs (and payloads) where the term occurs
difference between consecutive docIDs encoded to shrink postings
forward jump within a postings list to speed intersection
ordering postings by term weight for early-termination top-k
amortized merge schedule for incremental indexing
permanent lossy removal of low-value postings
document-to-terms mapping for snippets and features
compressed self-index using BWT and rank/select
character n-gram index for wildcard/fuzzy term match

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established IR indexing literature and engineering practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Build the dictionary plus postings lists that map each term to the documents (and optionally positions) containing it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when query mix shifts toward phrase/boolean workloads requiring richer postings payloads

pros.claim: baseline structure that all retrieval ranking builds on
pros.example: a query for 'graph' resolves to its postings list in O(1) dictionary lookup

cons.claim: schema choices here propagate to compression, skip, and positional layers
cons.example: choosing fixed-width docIDs blocks later gap-delta compression

failure_modes: dictionary cannot fit in memory for large vocabulary
docID ordering not gap-friendly downstream
acceptance_tests: dictionary lookup returns correct postings for sampled terms
revisit_triggers: vocabulary growth exceeds dictionary memory budget

nodes.definition: Assign integer document identifiers and choose a global ordering that maximizes gap compressibility and skip efficiency.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when measured gap distribution shows clustering ordering would cut postings size materially

pros.claim: clustered docIDs shrink d-gaps and improve VByte/PForDelta ratios
pros.example: URL-sorted web docIDs reduce gaps so gamma codes shorten

cons.claim: reordering invalidates externally stored docID references
cons.example: reassigning docIDs breaks cached result snippets keyed by old IDs

failure_modes: reorder breaks stable external docID contracts
optimization cost exceeds compression gain
acceptance_tests: gap entropy after reorder <= arrival-order baseline
revisit_triggers: external systems depend on docID stability

nodes.definition: Encode docID gaps and frequencies with integer codes (gamma, delta, variable-byte, PForDelta, Simple9/16) to shrink postings while keeping decode fast.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when decode-speed profiling shows a SIMD codec (PForDelta) beats current code on the workload

pros.claim: cuts index size several-fold and improves cache residency
pros.example: VByte stores small gaps in one byte, shrinking common-term postings

cons.claim: bit-aligned codes (gamma/delta) decode slower than byte/SIMD codes
cons.example: gamma decode branch-misprediction dominates hot postings traversal

failure_modes: codec mismatch with skip-pointer block boundaries
exception handling in PForDelta overflows
revisit_triggers: new codec available with better speed/size frontier

nodes.definition: Insert forward skip pointers into postings so conjunctive intersection can jump past non-matching docIDs without full scans.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when intersection profiling shows skip interval is far from sqrt(L) optimum

pros.claim: turns conjunctive intersection sublinear for selective terms
pros.example: intersecting 'the' AND 'quokka' skips most of the long 'the' list

cons.claim: skips add space and help little on dense or disjunctive queries
cons.example: fine skip intervals waste space when both lists are short

failure_modes: skip granularity misaligned with compression blocks
skips ignored by disjunctive WAND traversal
acceptance_tests: skip-based intersection equals linear-merge result set
revisit_triggers: query workload shifts to disjunctive scoring

nodes.definition: Store within-document term positions in postings so phrase and proximity queries can verify adjacency.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when phrase/proximity query share rises enough to justify positional payload cost

pros.claim: enables exact phrase and proximity scoring without false positives
pros.example: "new york" verified by adjacent positions, not just co-occurrence

cons.claim: positional payloads inflate index size and slow decode
cons.example: storing positions can multiply postings size for verbose fields

failure_modes: position payloads overflow block codec
phrase verify ignored, returning co-occurrence false hits
acceptance_tests: phrase results contain only adjacency-verified docs
revisit_triggers: phrase query share drops, payload cost no longer justified

nodes.definition: Index consecutive term pairs (biwords) as dictionary keys to answer common two-word phrases without positions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when two-word phrases dominate query logs and positional cost is prohibitive

pros.claim: answers frequent two-word phrases with a single dictionary lookup
pros.example: 'stanford university' resolves via one biword key, no position merge

cons.claim: vocabulary explodes and long phrases still need positions
cons.example: biword dictionary grows quadratically with term co-occurrence

failure_modes: biword vocabulary blowup
longer phrases silently degrade to AND
acceptance_tests: biword phrase results match positional ground truth on sample
revisit_triggers: phrase length distribution shifts beyond two words

nodes.definition: Order or tier postings by per-document impact (term weight) so top-k ranking can stop early without scanning full lists.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when top-k latency dominates and ranking model exposes stable impact bounds

pros.claim: enables safe early termination for top-k, cutting scan cost
pros.example: champion lists answer top-10 by touching only high-impact prefixes

cons.claim: impact order breaks docID-gap compression and conjunctive skips
cons.example: impact-sorted postings lose monotonic docIDs, hurting VByte gaps

failure_modes: early termination drops true top-k (unsafe pruning)
tier boundaries stale after ranking model change
acceptance_tests: early-terminated top-k matches exhaustive top-k on eval set

nodes.definition: Choose document-at-a-time vs term-at-a-time traversal and dynamic pruning (WAND/MaxScore) consistent with the index layout.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when block-max metadata becomes available enabling BlockMax-WAND

pros.claim: dynamic pruning skips low-scoring docs for large speedups
pros.example: BlockMax-WAND skips whole blocks below the heap threshold

cons.claim: pruning correctness depends on tight, layout-consistent score bounds
cons.example: loose max-score upper bounds make WAND prune too little or unsafely

failure_modes: score upper bounds inconsistent with index, breaking safety
pruning strategy mismatched to layout (impact vs docID)
acceptance_tests: WAND top-k equals exhaustive top-k on eval set
revisit_triggers: layout switches between docID and impact ordering

nodes.definition: Build the initial index from a corpus using a scalable external-memory algorithm (BSBI block sort or SPIMI single-pass in-memory).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when corpus size exceeds RAM, forcing SPIMI/BSBI external strategy choice

pros.claim: scales index build beyond RAM via blocking and external merge
pros.example: SPIMI writes per-block dictionaries then merges, avoiding global term map

cons.claim: build choices constrain later dynamic-update and partitioning design
cons.example: a BSBI global term-ID map complicates incremental SPIMI updates

failure_modes: intermediate spill exceeds disk
term-ID assignment race in parallel blocks
acceptance_tests: rebuilt index equals reference index on sample queries
revisit_triggers: corpus size or memory budget changes
downstream update model requires different layout

nodes.definition: Build and serve the index across machines via MapReduce-style construction and a term- vs document-partitioning choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when query latency vs throughput tradeoff shifts the partitioning regime

pros.claim: scales beyond one machine and parallelizes per-query work
pros.example: document-partitioning lets each shard score its docs independently

cons.claim: term-partitioning concentrates hot-term load; doc-partitioning multiplies query fanout
cons.example: a single hot term overloads its node under term-partitioning

failure_modes: skewed shard load (hot terms/docs)
scatter-gather tail latency from slowest shard
acceptance_tests: distributed top-k equals single-node top-k on sample

nodes.definition: Support incremental document add/delete via an auxiliary index plus logarithmic merge and deletion handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when update rate rises so merge amortization parameters must be retuned

pros.claim: absorbs updates without full rebuild via amortized merges
pros.example: logarithmic merge keeps amortized indexing cost low under steady updates

cons.claim: merges cause query-time fragmentation and transient stale results
cons.example: queries during a large merge may miss just-deleted docs

failure_modes: merge thrash under high update rate
deleted docs leak into results before merge
revisit_triggers: update rate or doc churn changes
merge latency impacts query freshness SLO

nodes.definition: Permanently drop low-value postings entries (term- or document-centric) to shrink the index with bounded ranking loss.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when measured top-k quality loss from pruning crosses the acceptable budget

pros.claim: shrinks index and speeds queries with bounded quality loss
pros.example: term-centric pruning drops tail postings unlikely to affect top-10

cons.claim: pruning is irreversible and can silently degrade tail/recall queries
cons.example: aggressive pruning removes the only postings answering rare queries

failure_modes: pruning removes postings needed for rare but important queries
quality regression undetected without eval set
acceptance_tests: top-k quality delta within configured budget on eval set
revisit_triggers: query distribution changes exposing pruned terms

nodes.definition: Maintain a document-to-terms mapping for snippet generation, re-ranking features, and index rebuild support.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when re-ranking or snippet features require per-document term access

pros.claim: supports snippets and feature re-ranking the inverted index cannot
pros.example: forward index yields document term vector for learned re-ranking

cons.claim: duplicates storage and must stay consistent with inverted index
cons.example: forward and inverted indexes can diverge after partial update

failure_modes: forward/inverted divergence after update
stored-field bloat
acceptance_tests: forward index doc count matches inverted index
snippet terms present in source doc

nodes.definition: Build a suffix array (optionally with LCP) for arbitrary substring and pattern search over text not naturally tokenized into terms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when substring/non-tokenized search (DNA, code, CJK) is required

pros.claim: answers arbitrary substring queries token indexes cannot
pros.example: suffix array finds any infix in genomic text via binary search

cons.claim: construction and memory are heavy versus inverted indexes
cons.example: naive suffix array build is costly; compressed variants add complexity

failure_modes: construction memory blowup on large alphabets
unsuitable for ranked term retrieval
acceptance_tests: pattern search returns all and only occurrences
array is a valid suffix permutation
revisit_triggers: text becomes tokenizable, favoring inverted index

nodes.definition: Use a wavelet tree to provide compressed rank/select over symbol sequences enabling FM-index-style backward search.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when index must be both searchable and near entropy-compressed in memory

pros.claim: self-index: search a compressed sequence without decompressing
pros.example: FM-index backward search counts pattern occurrences in compressed space

cons.claim: complex to implement and tune versus mature inverted pipelines
cons.example: rank/select constant factors can be high without engineering care

failure_modes: rank/select constants make queries slow
implementation bugs in succinct bitvectors
acceptance_tests: rank/select agree with brute-force on sample

nodes.definition: Index character k-grams to support wildcard, spelling-tolerant, and substring term matching via gram intersection plus post-filtering.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when wildcard/fuzzy query share rises enough to justify gram index cost

pros.claim: answers wildcard and fuzzy term queries via gram intersection
pros.example: 're* val' matches via shared trigrams then verifies candidates

cons.claim: gram intersection yields false positives needing post-filtering
cons.example: trigram match returns spurious terms requiring regex verify

failure_modes: candidate explosion for short wildcards
missing post-filter returns wrong terms
acceptance_tests: wildcard results equal regex ground truth after post-filter

nodes.definition: Maintain hashed bit-signatures per document for fast membership pre-filtering, accepting false positives resolved downstream.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a memory-light approximate pre-filter is preferable to full postings

pros.claim: compact membership pre-filter for some workloads
pros.example: a signature scan rejects most non-matching docs before postings lookup

cons.claim: false positives and poor ranking support vs inverted index
cons.example: signature false-positive rate forces costly verification passes

failure_modes: false-positive rate too high
does not support ranked retrieval
acceptance_tests: no false negatives on membership sample
revisit_triggers: false-positive rate degrades with collection growth

nodes.definition: Cache hot postings lists and full query results across the memory hierarchy with eviction and invalidation policies.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when query locality or update rate shifts the optimal cache tier mix

pros.claim: large latency cuts for repeated queries and hot terms
pros.example: a result cache serves popular head queries in microseconds

cons.claim: stale results after updates unless invalidation is correct
cons.example: result cache returns pre-update hits after a document is deleted

failure_modes: stale cache after index update
cache thrash under low-locality workload
acceptance_tests: cached result equals freshly computed result post-invalidation
hit rate meets target on replayed log
revisit_triggers: update rate rises, invalidation cost grows

nodes.definition: Validate index correctness, size, decode/query latency, and ranking-quality preservation across all structural choices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any structural change (codec, pruning, ordering) requires re-benchmarking before lock

pros.claim: prevents shipping size/speed wins that silently break correctness or ranking
pros.example: catches that impact-ordering broke conjunctive recall before release

cons.claim: comprehensive eval is slow and gates iteration speed
cons.example: full size/speed/quality sweep delays each index change

failure_modes: eval set unrepresentative of production queries
quality regression masked by aggregate metric
acceptance_tests: correctness oracle passes on all variants
quality delta within budget vs baseline
revisit_triggers: eval set or relevance judgments updated

edges.why_related: docID assignment operates on the term-document space defined by the inverted index core
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stable docID space enables gap-friendly ordering
edges.example: core index must exist before docIDs can be permuted
edges.resolution_rule: finalize core docID space before ordering experiments

edges.why_related: compression encodes the postings produced by the core index
edges.benefit_of_coupling: baseline postings define what is compressed
edges.example: build core postings before choosing codecs
edges.resolution_rule: keep core layout draft until codec chosen

edges.why_related: docID ordering changes gap distribution that compression exploits
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clustered docIDs shrink gaps and compressed size
edges.example: URL-sorted docIDs cut gamma-coded size
edges.resolution_rule: fix docID ordering before encoding postings; reorder triggers re-encode

edges.why_related: skip pointers are placed over compressed postings blocks
edges.risk_of_conflict: misaligned skips and blocks corrupt traversal
edges.example: skip offsets must match PForDelta block starts
edges.resolution_rule: align skip granularity to compression block boundaries

edges.why_related: docID-gap compression assumes monotonic docIDs while impact ordering reorders by weight
edges.benefit_of_coupling: either small postings or fast top-k, not both freely
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing impact order degrades gap compression
edges.example: impact-sorted postings lose docID monotonicity, hurting VByte
edges.resolution_rule: if top-k latency dominates choose impact order in a tier; else keep docID-ordered compressed list; may store both

edges.why_related: DAAT conjunctive traversal uses skip pointers to advance lists
edges.example: WAND ignores skips on dense lists
edges.resolution_rule: use skips for conjunctive DAAT; fall back to linear merge when lists short

edges.why_related: early-termination query processing consumes impact-ordered postings/tiers
edges.benefit_of_coupling: impact layout enables safe early stop
edges.example: BlockMax-WAND needs per-block max scores
edges.resolution_rule: rebuild query bounds whenever tiers/impacts change

edges.why_related: impact-ordering layout constrains which pruning algorithm is safe
edges.example: MaxScore needs tight upper bounds from the layout
edges.resolution_rule: score upper bounds must be derived from the actual postings layout

edges.why_related: positional payloads extend the core postings with position lists
edges.example: adding positions multiplies postings size
edges.resolution_rule: add positions as optional payload; gate on phrase query share

edges.why_related: positional phrase verification and biword dictionary are competing phrase strategies
edges.benefit_of_coupling: pick the cheaper strategy for the phrase-length distribution
edges.example: two-word phrases via biword vs positions
edges.resolution_rule: use biword for dominant short phrases, positions for long/arbitrary phrases; avoid maintaining both fully

edges.why_related: position payloads constrain the codec since positions need their own encoding
edges.benefit_of_coupling: good codec keeps positional size bounded
edges.example: positions need separate gap encoding within block
edges.resolution_rule: choose a codec that encodes position payloads, not only docID gaps

edges.why_related: the core index schema constrains which construction algorithm and layout are valid
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fixed core schema lets the build target a stable layout
edges.risk_of_conflict: build assumptions drifting from core schema force rework
edges.example: core dictionary/postings layout dictates SPIMI block dictionary format
edges.resolution_rule: fix core schema before selecting BSBI vs SPIMI build; schema changes re-open build design

edges.why_related: distributed indexing generalizes single-node construction across machines
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared build logic reused per shard
edges.example: BSBI merge logic reused inside MapReduce reduce
edges.resolution_rule: validate single-node build before distributing

edges.why_related: dynamic indexing layers incremental merges on the constructed index
edges.risk_of_conflict: layout hostile to merge forces rebuild
edges.example: global term-IDs complicate incremental merge
edges.resolution_rule: choose build layout that supports incremental merge before committing

edges.why_related: partitioning scheme and incremental merge policy contend over shard locality and merge scope
edges.benefit_of_coupling: coordinated design avoids cross-shard merge storms
edges.example: doc-partitioning eases local merges; term-partitioning forces cross-node merges
edges.resolution_rule: prefer document-partitioning when incremental merge is frequent; record decision

edges.why_related: partitioning constrains docID ranges and thus gap compression per shard
edges.benefit_of_coupling: per-shard local docIDs keep gaps small
edges.risk_of_conflict: global docIDs across shards enlarge gaps
edges.example: local shard docIDs compress better than global
edges.resolution_rule: use shard-local docID spaces to preserve gap compression

edges.why_related: static pruning uses impact scores to decide which postings to drop
edges.benefit_of_coupling: impacts guide which entries are low-value
edges.risk_of_conflict: pruning without impacts drops useful postings
edges.example: term-centric pruning ranks by impact
edges.resolution_rule: compute impacts before pruning decisions

edges.why_related: compression is lossless size reduction while static pruning is lossy reduction; both target size
edges.benefit_of_coupling: combine for max size reduction within quality budget
edges.example: pruned then compressed index may breach recall budget
edges.resolution_rule: apply pruning only within validated quality budget; compression is preferred lossless reduction first

edges.why_related: validation must confirm pruning's ranking-quality loss is within budget
edges.example: pruning shipped without eval drops rare-query recall
edges.resolution_rule: no pruning may finalize before quality eval passes

edges.why_related: validation confirms dynamic pruning returns the same top-k as exhaustive scoring
edges.example: WAND bug drops a relevant doc undetected
edges.resolution_rule: validate top-k equivalence before enabling pruning in production

edges.why_related: validation benchmarks decode speed and round-trip correctness of codecs
edges.example: codec edge case corrupts a postings list
edges.resolution_rule: codec must pass round-trip and latency benchmarks before lock

edges.why_related: forward index is built alongside the core index over the same documents
edges.example: partial update leaves forward stale
edges.resolution_rule: update forward and inverted indexes transactionally

edges.why_related: both store per-document term detail though for different access patterns
edges.example: forward term vectors overlap positional needs
edges.resolution_rule: deduplicate per-document term storage where access patterns permit

edges.why_related: FM-index search via wavelet tree is built from BWT derived from the suffix array
edges.benefit_of_coupling: SA gives the BWT for the index
edges.example: large-text SA build limits FM-index scale
edges.resolution_rule: build/validate suffix array before constructing the wavelet/FM-index

edges.why_related: both support substring/pattern matching beyond exact terms
edges.benefit_of_coupling: choose by query class and cost
edges.example: suffix array and n-gram both match infixes
edges.resolution_rule: prefer n-gram index for tokenized terms; suffix array for raw sequence

edges.why_related: n-gram/wildcard index maps grams to dictionary terms of the core index
edges.risk_of_conflict: candidate terms must exist in core dictionary
edges.example: wildcard expands to core dictionary terms
edges.resolution_rule: build gram index over the finalized term dictionary

edges.why_related: wildcard term expansion constrains downstream phrase verification cost
edges.benefit_of_coupling: bounded expansion keeps phrase cost sane
edges.risk_of_conflict: huge expansion blows up phrase verify
edges.example: wildcard in a phrase explodes positional checks
edges.resolution_rule: cap wildcard expansion before phrase verification

edges.why_related: signature files and inverted index are competing membership structures with different cost/quality
edges.benefit_of_coupling: signature pre-filter can cut postings lookups
edges.risk_of_conflict: signatures add false positives and weak ranking
edges.example: signature scan vs postings lookup for membership
edges.resolution_rule: use inverted index for ranked retrieval; signatures only as memory-light pre-filter when justified

edges.why_related: postings cache stores decoded/compressed hot lists from the codec
edges.example: re-encoded list invalidates cached blocks
edges.resolution_rule: invalidate postings cache on codec or list change

edges.why_related: incremental updates threaten result-cache freshness creating staleness pressure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cache gives latency wins; updates demand invalidation
edges.example: deleted doc still served from result cache
edges.resolution_rule: on each merge/delete, invalidate affected cache entries before serving; correctness over hit-rate

edges.why_related: validation confirms post-merge results reflect adds/deletes
edges.example: stale postings returned after merge
edges.resolution_rule: validate deletion visibility after each merge policy change

edges.why_related: validation confirms distributed top-k equals single-node top-k
edges.example: missing shard silently lowers recall
edges.resolution_rule: validate distributed vs single-node equivalence before scaling out

edges.why_related: cache hit-rate telemetry can trigger revisiting traversal/pruning strategy
edges.example: cache miss spike prompts pruning retune
edges.resolution_rule: revisit query processing only when hit-rate change exceeds materiality threshold; stop after 2 retunes

edges.why_related: quality-regression findings trigger revisiting/rolling back pruning aggressiveness
edges.example: eval shows recall loss, prune less
edges.resolution_rule: loosen pruning when quality delta exceeds budget; stop when within budget or after 3 iterations

edges.why_related: benchmark results trigger revisiting codec choice on the speed/size frontier
edges.example: latency miss prompts SIMD codec switch
edges.resolution_rule: switch codec only on benchmark delta above threshold; stop after frontier reached

edges.why_related: docID ordering affects how effectively skip pointers prune during intersection
edges.example: reorder shifts skip target offsets
edges.resolution_rule: recompute skip layout whenever docID ordering changes

edges.why_related: both expand the dictionary key space for richer term matching
edges.example: biword plus gram keys inflate dictionary
edges.resolution_rule: bound combined auxiliary key growth against dictionary budget

edges.why_related: both pursue compressed representations of index data
edges.example: succinct and integer-coding overlap
edges.resolution_rule: treat as alternative compressed-index regimes; pick by query class

edges.why_related: validation measures signature false-positive rate against budget
edges.example: unvalidated signatures over-filter
edges.resolution_rule: validate false-positive/negative rates before adopting signatures

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing a codec/skip layout that minimizes size but slows decode/intersection
resolution_order: benchmark decode throughput vs size
pick frontier point meeting latency SLO
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: latency SLO dominates: never trade below the decode-speed threshold required by query latency
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no codec meets both size and latency SLO simultaneously
conflict_axes.example: bit-aligned gamma is smaller but slower than SIMD PForDelta

conflict_axes.trigger: top-k workload wants impact ordering but gap compression wants monotonic docIDs
resolution_order: measure top-k latency need vs compression loss
choose per-list ordering or dual layout
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if top-k latency dominates use impact-ordered tier; else keep docID-ordered compressed list
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when both compression budget and top-k latency SLO are violated

conflict_axes.trigger: phrase queries can be served by positions or biword keys with different cost profiles
resolution_order: analyze phrase-length distribution
pick positions for arbitrary, biword for dominant short phrases
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: positions dominate for arbitrary-length/proximity; biword only when short phrases dominate and space allows
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when phrase-length distribution is unknown or shifting
conflict_axes.example: "new york city" needs positions, biword only covers pairs

conflict_axes.trigger: both reduce index size; pruning is irreversible and risks ranking quality
resolution_order: apply lossless compression first
apply pruning only within validated quality budget
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: lossless compression dominates; lossy pruning subordinate and gated by quality eval
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when size target unreachable without breaching quality budget
conflict_axes.example: pruning then compressing may breach recall budget

conflict_axes.trigger: term-partitioning concentrates hot-term load; document-partitioning multiplies query fanout
resolution_order: model hot-term skew and query fanout
default to document-partitioning unless throughput dictates otherwise
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: document-partitioning dominates for tail-latency and incremental merge; term-partitioning only for specific throughput cases
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when shard load skew exceeds tolerance under either scheme
conflict_axes.example: single hot term overloads its node under term-partitioning

conflict_axes.trigger: incremental updates require cache invalidation that lowers hit rate
resolution_order: invalidate affected entries on merge/delete
measure freshness vs hit-rate tradeoff
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: result correctness/freshness dominates cache hit-rate; serve stale never preferred
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when invalidation cost makes caching net-negative
conflict_axes.example: deleted doc served from stale result cache

conflict_axes.trigger: a build layout optimized for batch may be hostile to incremental merges
resolution_order: choose layout supporting incremental merge if update rate high
else optimize batch build
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if sustained updates expected, merge-friendly layout dominates batch-build optimality
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when neither full rebuild nor incremental merge meets freshness SLO
conflict_axes.example: global term-IDs complicate incremental SPIMI updates

conflict_axes.trigger: non-term or membership workloads tempt specialized structures over the inverted index
resolution_order: classify query type (term/substring/membership)
use inverted index for ranked term retrieval by default
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: inverted index dominates ranked term retrieval; specialized indexes only for substring/membership niches
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when query class is mixed and neither structure dominates
conflict_axes.example: signature files lack ranking; suffix array heavy for term retrieval

conflict_axes.trigger: adding payloads/tiers enriches answers but enlarges postings and decode cost
resolution_order: gate each payload on measured query-share benefit
drop payloads not justified by query mix
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: query latency SLO dominates speculative feature richness
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when added features push latency past SLO
conflict_axes.example: positional payloads slow decode for rarely-phrased fields

conflict_axes.trigger: full size/speed/quality eval slows each index change
resolution_order: run fast correctness oracle every change
run full quality sweep before lock
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correctness+quality validation dominates iteration speed before any production lock
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when eval backlog blocks a critical fix
conflict_axes.example: skipping eval shipped impact-ordering that broke conjunctive recall

edge_cases.trigger: docID reassignment without updating external references
edge_cases.failure_mode: cached snippets/results key on stale docIDs
edge_cases.example: reorder breaks cached result docID keys
edge_cases.detection_method: diff docID map version against references stored in cache/forward index
resolution: invalidate caches keyed on old docIDs

edge_cases.trigger: skip offsets not aligned to codec block boundaries
edge_cases.detection_method: assert skip targets land on block starts during build
resolution: align skip interval to block size

edge_cases.trigger: early termination with loose score upper bounds
edge_cases.detection_method: compare pruned top-k against exhaustive top-k on eval set

edge_cases.trigger: static pruning removes postings for rare important queries
edge_cases.failure_mode: irreversible recall loss on tail queries
edge_cases.example: rare query loses its only postings
deleted doc still returned from cache
edge_cases.detection_method: replay update then query; compare cached vs fresh result

edge_cases.trigger: modeling construction as both producing and depending on the core schema
edge_cases.failure_mode: dependency cycle blocks topological build order
edge_cases.detection_method: run dependency-cycle check over node deps and dependency edges
resolution: keep core schema as upstream prerequisite

edge_cases.trigger: hot term or hot doc concentrated on one shard
edge_cases.failure_mode: tail latency dominated by overloaded shard
edge_cases.example: single hot term saturates its node
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor per-shard load distribution under replayed query log

edge_cases.trigger: partial update applied to one index but not the other
edge_cases.detection_method: reconcile doc counts and term presence between indexes

edge_cases.trigger: short wildcard expands to enormous candidate set
edge_cases.example: 'a*' expands to most of the dictionary
edge_cases.detection_method: bound candidate set size and measure verify cost

edge_cases.trigger: signature false-positive rate grows with collection size
edge_cases.example: signature scan yields mostly false hits
edge_cases.detection_method: measure false-positive rate vs budget as collection grows
resolution: widen signatures or abandon for inverted index

edge_cases.trigger: computed size/speed score labeled observed without measurement
edge_cases.failure_mode: heuristic estimate overclaimed as observed evidence
edge_cases.detection_method: check evidence labels against availability of measured data

edge_cases.trigger: FM-index built from outdated suffix array after text change
edge_cases.failure_mode: backward search returns positions for stale text
edge_cases.example: edited document not reflected in FM-index
edge_cases.detection_method: version text and rebuild SA/wavelet on change
resolution: rebuild suffix array and wavelet tree on text edit

workflow.objective: fix core inverted-index schema, docID space, and competency questions
acceptance_tests: dictionary lookup returns correct postings on sample
workflow.do_first_because: core schema and docID space are highest-coupling foundations all later structures depend on

workflow.objective: choose integer codecs and skip layout on the size/speed frontier
workflow.do_first_because: compression layout constrains skip, impact, and positional design; settle before downstream layers

workflow.objective: decide phrase, proximity, and wildcard payload structures per query mix
acceptance_tests: wildcard results match regex ground truth
workflow.do_first_because: payload choices depend on core+compression but are independent of ranking layout, enabling parallelism

workflow.objective: design impact ordering/tiers and dynamic-pruning traversal for top-k
acceptance_tests: pruned top-k equals exhaustive top-k on eval set
workflow.do_first_because: ranking layout conflicts with docID-gap compression; design after compression is settled

workflow.objective: implement scalable single-node build (BSBI/SPIMI) honoring the core schema
acceptance_tests: rebuilt index matches reference on sample
workflow.do_first_because: construction must produce a correct core index before distribution and incremental updates are layered

workflow.objective: partition and distribute construction/serving across machines
acceptance_tests: distributed top-k equals single-node top-k on sample
workflow.do_first_because: distribution depends on a validated single-node build and a chosen partitioning regime

workflow.objective: add incremental update via auxiliary index, logarithmic merge, and deletions
workflow.do_first_because: incremental updates depend on a stable build layout and interact with partitioning and caching

workflow.objective: build forward index and any specialized text/membership indexes the workload needs
exit_criteria: needed auxiliary indexes built and validated
workflow.do_first_because: auxiliary/text indexes depend on core but are independent of ranking/distribution, enabling parallel work

workflow.objective: apply lossless compression fully then lossy pruning within validated quality budget
acceptance_tests: top-k quality delta within budget on eval set
exit_criteria: human review of irreversible drop done
workflow.do_first_because: pruning is irreversible and lossy; it must follow lossless compression and precede final validation/lock

workflow.objective: benchmark size/speed/quality, configure caching+invalidation, and decide production lock
acceptance_tests: cache result equals fresh result post-invalidation
workflow.do_first_because: hard lock only after dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass per lock policy

priority_rationale.notes: core schema all structures depend on
docID ordering drives compression and skips
must build a correct core index before scaling/updates
partitioning is hard to change later
gates all irreversible/lossy changes before lock

dominance_rules.trigger: an index change improves latency/size but risks correctness or recall
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a size/speed win that fails correctness or quality validation
dominance_rules.example: impact-ordering speedup rejected because conjunctive recall dropped

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks a finalized prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: do not finalize a node before its dependencies are reviewed
dominance_rules.required_action: reorder execution to satisfy dependencies first
dominance_rules.example: pruning deferred until impacts and compression are settled

dominance_rules.trigger: a size/speed/quality figure is stated more precisely than its evidence supports
dominance_rules.rule: label estimates heuristic until measured; never overclaim observed
dominance_rules.example: estimated decode speed kept heuristic, not observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a variant is proposed for hard lock before benchmarks complete
dominance_rules.rule: no hard lock before correctness, quality, and freshness gates pass
dominance_rules.required_action: hold lock until validation_report.hard_lock_allowed is true
dominance_rules.example: release blocked until benchmark frontier verified

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible pruning or partitioning decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: irreversible/lossy decisions require human review before commit
dominance_rules.required_action: route to human-review gate with decision record
dominance_rules.example: pruning that removes tail postings gets human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to add many structures before the core schema stabilizes
dominance_rules.rule: stabilize core schema and docID space before populating downstream structures
dominance_rules.required_action: soft-lock core schema before payload/ranking design
dominance_rules.example: defer positional payloads until core layout frozen

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting conflicts with strict JSON
dominance_rules.rule: valid machine-parseable JSON dominates descriptive richness
dominance_rules.required_action: drop prose that threatens JSON validity
dominance_rules.example: compact field text over verbose explanation

dominance_rules.trigger: a benefit is asserted without measurement or eligible source
dominance_rules.rule: every quantitative claim must trace to an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs or downgrade the claim
dominance_rules.example: compression-ratio claim tied to SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR until benchmarked

dominance_rules.trigger: adding index features pushes query latency past SLO
dominance_rules.rule: latency/space budget dominates speculative feature richness
dominance_rules.required_action: drop features not justified by measured query share
dominance_rules.example: remove positional payload for rarely-phrased fields

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal codec choice would force downstream re-encode
dominance_rules.rule: sequence decisions to avoid downstream rework even if locally suboptimal
dominance_rules.required_action: fix docID ordering before codec selection
dominance_rules.example: avoid reorder after compression by ordering first

dominance_rules.trigger: a score is produced without exposing its input variables
dominance_rules.rule: all scores must derive from explicit, labeled input variables
dominance_rules.required_action: store AT/DG/UR/RT and metric inputs before computing scores

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing introduces a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.rule: dependency graph must stay acyclic; convert weaker links to sequence/constraint
dominance_rules.required_action: model core schema as upstream of construction, not mutual
dominance_rules.example: construction depends on core, not vice versa

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve corpus/query scope before locking core schema
anti_rework_rules.rationale: schema built on wrong scope forces full redesign
anti_rework_rules.example: positional payload added then dropped after profiling

anti_rework_rules.rule: derive competency questions before populating structures
anti_rework_rules.rationale: structures unaligned to questions are wasted work
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: nodes added with no competency-question reference
anti_rework_rules.example: wildcard index built with no fuzzy-query requirement

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix docID ordering before selecting postings codecs
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reordering after encoding forces re-encode of all postings
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: docID reorder proposed after codec lock

anti_rework_rules.rule: stabilize core postings layout before compression design
anti_rework_rules.rationale: compressing an unstable layout invalidates encoded blocks
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: codec chosen while core layout still draft
anti_rework_rules.example: skip layout redone after schema change

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle compression before designing impact/ranking layout
anti_rework_rules.rationale: impact ordering conflicts with gap compression; sequence avoids thrash
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: ranking layout changed after impact-vs-gap conflict surfaced
anti_rework_rules.example: impact order chosen then reverted for compression

anti_rework_rules.rationale: distributing a buggy build multiplies and hides defects
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scale-out begun with failing build correctness

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix build layout before designing incremental merge
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: merge policy designed before layout chosen

anti_rework_rules.rule: apply lossless compression before lossy pruning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: pruning is irreversible; do reversible reductions first
anti_rework_rules.example: recall lost to pruning that compression would have avoided

anti_rework_rules.rule: run full validation before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking unvalidated variants ships silent regressions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard lock requested with hard_lock_allowed false

anti_rework_rules.rule: wire cache invalidation before enabling caching under updates
anti_rework_rules.rationale: caching without invalidation serves stale results
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: cache enabled with no update->invalidation path

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete traceability matrix before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unverified linkage hides unsupported objects at lock time
anti_rework_rules.example: node lacks source/CQ linkage at release

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or benchmark reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report and benchmark deltas to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node

acceptance_tests: fix addresses root cause not symptom

iteration_protocol.trigger: new measurement or evidence becomes available
a dependency cycle or invalid edge ref is found
an upstream change invalidates a locked artifact
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked artifact depends on changed upstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk>0.80 or confidence<0.65 or irreversible decision
acceptance_tests: human sign-off recorded for high-risk items

iteration_protocol.detection: compare against prior index variant baseline
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: candidate dominates or matches baseline within budget

human_review_required_for: hard lock of any index variant

checks.repair_action: scores computed by formula script within tol 0.02

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked structural change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when evidence label is revised
